text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.4% today as oil prices spiked sharply on escalating geopolitical tension in the Middle East. Iran intensified attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday, a critical chokepoint for global oil supplies, pushing U.S. crude toward $102 a barrel and Brent crude to $110. For an oil producer like ConocoPhillips, higher oil prices directly translate to higher revenues and profits, which is why the stock accelerated higher over the past week alongside the price move — the stock is up nearly 16% in two weeks as geopolitical risk has pushed crude meaningfully higher.

Beyond the day's headlines, traders are also pricing in a structural mismatch between what oil costs to produce and deliver versus the headline price. Tanker rates have surged so much that the actual cost to physically move crude to market is roughly $38 per barrel higher than the spot price suggests, meaning the real margin for producers is wider than the raw numbers imply. Combined with drone and missile threats to refinery capacity in the region, this creates both upside for producers and potential supply tightness that reinforces the price floor.
